Inflection Points of Fourth Degree Polynomials

CurvesAlgebraLimits
Game: A curve with a wiggle has two points where it changes its bend; a line through them meets the curve twice more. There is nothing to win or lose.
How to play: Move the five sliders to change the curve and read the numbers under the picture.

Look for the math

A quartic p(x) = m₄x⁴ + m₃x³ + m₂x² + m₁x + m₀ may have two inflection points a < b, where p″ changes sign. Draw the line L through them.

The line meets the graph twice more

Write p″ = 12m₄(x − a)(x − b) and integrate: p − L has the coefficients m₄, −2(a+b)m₄, 6ab·m₄, (a³ − 3a²b − 3ab² + b³)m₄, −ab(a² − 3ab + b²)m₄, and the roots xL, a, b, xR. Comparing with the factored form gives a + b = xL + xR and xLxR = −(a² − 3ab + b²), so xL, xR = ((a+b) ∓ (b−a)√5)/2.

The golden ratio

That makes (b − a)/(a − xL) = (1 + √5)/2, the golden ratio. Also a − xL = xR − b, so p − L is symmetric: tick Difference. The three regions between graph and line have areas in the ratio 1 : 2 : 1. The logic test checked all of it on 200,000 random quartics, the areas by exact integration.

The slider range (−10 to 10 in steps of 0.1) is my choice; the applet's sliders have a movable origin and unit. Without two inflection points (m₄ = 0, or p″ with no two real roots) there is no line.

Keep m₄ = 1 and move m₂ from −6 towards 0: what happens to the two inflection points?
